trust_decision.summary: The multipart body processor decides a part's filename solely from mime.ParseMediaType's plain "filename" parameter, so an RFC 5987 "filename*" carrying a charset the Go stdlib does not special-case (anything other than us-ascii/utf-8) is dropped silently and the attacker's decoy plain filename is what every FILES/FILES_SIZES/MULTIPART_FILENAME rule sees; the decision is made in originFileName, called from multipartBodyProcessor.ProcessRequest.

landing_point.why: originFileName is the only place a multipart part's filename is derived; every value written to FILES, FILES_SIZES and (once populated) MULTIPART_FILENAME comes from it, and it returns only dispositionParams["filename"] from mime.ParseMediaType.

fix_sites.entry_point: coraza.NewWAF(seclang config) with SecRule MULTIPART_FILENAME/_NAME/_CHARSET targets
public Go API for rule/variable names

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The new anomaly flags only feed a logdata line in an example config, so initialising them to "0" in WAF.newTransaction is cosmetic; the value comes from the multipart parser, which is where the fix belongs.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An ordinary single-filename upload must keep exactly one FILES value, one FILES_SIZES key and one Part-J uploaded-files row; adding the second reading unconditionally (or when it equals the first) double-counts the same bytes in the audit-log Total and breaks rules that assume one FILES entry per part.

O6_input_shapes: "filename" plus "filename*" with the decoy in filename and the real name in filename* (iso-8859-1 and other non-utf-8 charsets)
the swapped order: real name in plain filename, decoy in filename*
"filename*" alone with no plain filename (still must be a file upload, not an ARGS_POST field)
"filename*" that decodes to the empty string (utf-8'') next to a plain filename
empty charset segment (''value) and optional language segment (charset'lang'value)
RFC 2231 numbered continuations: filename*0=, filename*0*=, and a continuation alongside a bare filename*
duplicate "filename" / duplicate "filename*" parameters in one Content-Disposition
duplicate whole part headers (two Content-Disposition, two Content-Type)
two distinct parts sharing one form name (multi-file input)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: parse the part's "name" parameter with the same raw-header helper instead of p.FormName()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: p.FormName() goes through the same mime.ParseMediaType path, so a duplicate or quoted "name" parameter is resolved just as silently; a maintainer hardening Content-Disposition would naturally normalise name too, since ARGS_POST and FILES_NAMES are keyed on it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Part J uploaded-files listing must list one row per distinct filename and keep Total honest when a part carries two readings
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the published fix deliberately puts two names for one part into FILES, so whoever wrote the audit-log half of the same change had to decide the de-duplication rule there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: export the Content-Disposition filename parser through plugintypes so third-party multipart body processors share it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the plugin hook is already public and the ADR frames this as ModSecurity parser parity, so publishing the helper as part of the public body-processor API is a natural next step.

O9_family: CWE-20 / CWE-436 multipart Content-Disposition parser differential (RFC 5987 filename* vs plain filename)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make filename* authoritative whenever it parses (decode the media type yourself and prefer it over filename), which relocates the decoy to the swapped direction and still leaves FILES with a single name.

out_of_scope_notes: fix_commits also carries cae3c740, an unrelated advisory's fix (GHSA-3c6w-j9xm-8h2h: unbounded response-body JSON recursion in internal/bodyprocessors/json.go plus the SecResponseBodyJsonDepthLimit directive); it is not part of this advisory and was not screened.
FILES is only ever stored under the empty key (internal/bodyprocessors/multipart.go:99), so a ModSecurity-style SecRule FILES:<filename> selector never matches anything; not pursued.

The request body processor is chosen from the first Content-Type header value (internal/corazawaf/transaction.go:1107-1110), so duplicate Content-Type headers can make Coraza pick a non-multipart parser where a backend picks multipart; outside this advisory's filename property, not pursued.
